# PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE

## This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 32

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 32] Contents of this Practice Direction

## EVIDENCE IN GENERAL

## 1.1 Rule 32.2 sets out how evidence is to be given and facts are to be proved.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.1 Rule 32.2 sets out how evidence is to be given and facts are to be proved.] 1.2 Evidence at a hearing other than the trial should normally be given by witness statement 1 (see paragraph 17 onwards). However a witness may give evidence by affidavit if he wishes to do so 2 (and see paragraph 1.4 below).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.1 Rule 32.2 sets out how evidence is to be given and facts are to be proved.] 1.3 Statements of case (see paragraph 26 onwards) and application notices 3 may also be used as evidence provided that their contents have been verified by a statement of truth 4 .

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.1 Rule 32.2 sets out how evidence is to be given and facts are to be proved.] (For information regarding evidence by deposition see Part 34 and Practice Direction 34A.)

## 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] (1) where sworn evidence is required by an enactment 5 , rule, order or practice direction, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] (2) in any application for a search order, a freezing injunction, or an order requiring an occupier to permit another to enter his land.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] (By rule 81.4(1), unless and to the extent that the court directs otherwise every contempt application must be supported by written evidence given by affidavit or affirmation.).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] 1.5 If a party believes that sworn evidence is required by a court in another jurisdiction for any purpose connected with the proceedings, he may apply to the court for a direction that evidence shall be given only by affidavit on any pre-trial applications.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] 1.6 The court may give a direction under rule 32.15 that evidence shall be given by affidavit instead of or in addition to a witness statement or statement of case:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] (1) on its own initiative, or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] (2) after any party has applied to the court for such a direction.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 1.4 Affidavits must be used as evidence in the following instances:] 1.7 An affidavit, where referred to in the Civil Procedure Rules or a practice direction, also means an affirmation unless the context requires otherwise.

## AFFIDAVITS

## Deponent

## 2 A deponent is a person who gives evidence by affidavit or affirmation.

## Heading

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] 3.1 The affidavit should be headed with the title of the proceedings (see paragraph 4 of Practice Direction 7A and paragraph 5 of Practice Direction 20); where the proceedings are between several parties with the same status it is sufficient to identify the parties as follows:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] 3.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page (and on the backsheet) there should be clearly written:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] (1) the party on whose behalf it is made,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] (2) the initials and surname of the deponent,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] (3) the number of the affidavit in relation to that deponent,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] (4) the identifying initials and number of each exhibit referred to, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] (5) the date sworn.

## Body of affidavit

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of affidavit] 4.1 The affidavit must, if practicable, be in the deponent’s own words, the affidavit should be expressed in the first person and the deponent should:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of affidavit] (1) commence ‘I (full name) of (address) state on oath ……’,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of affidavit] (2) if giving evidence in his professional, business or other occupational capacity, give the address at which he works in (1) above, the position he holds and the name of his firm or employer,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of affidavit] (3) give his occupation or, if he has none, his description, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of affidavit] (4) state if he is a party to the proceedings or employed by a party to the proceedings, if it be the case.

## 4.2 An affidavit must indicate:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 4.2 An affidavit must indicate:] (1) which of the statements in it are made from the deponent’s own knowledge and which are matters of information or belief, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 4.2 An affidavit must indicate:] (2) the source for any matters of information or belief.

## 4.3 Where a deponent:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 4.3 Where a deponent:] (1) refers to an exhibit or exhibits, he should state‘there is now shown to me marked ‘…’ the (description of exhibit)’, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 4.3 Where a deponent:] (2) makes more than one affidavit (to which there are exhibits) in the same proceedings, the numbering of the exhibits should run consecutively throughout and not start again with each affidavit.

## Jurat

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Jurat] 5.1 The jurat of an affidavit is a statement set out at the end of the document which authenticates the affidavit.

## 5.2 It must:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 5.2 It must:] (1) be signed by all deponents,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 5.2 It must:] (2) be completed and signed by the person before whom the affidavit was sworn whose name and qualification must be printed beneath his signature,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 5.2 It must:] (3) contain the full address of the person before whom the affidavit was sworn, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 5.2 It must:] (4) follow immediately on from the text and not be put on a separate page.

## Format of affidavits

## 6.1 An affidavit should:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (1) be produced on durable quality A4 paper with a 3.5cm margin,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (2) be fully legible and should normally be typed on one side of the paper only,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (3) where possible, be bound securely in a manner which would not hamper filing, or otherwise each page should be endorsed with the case number and should bear the initials of the deponent and of the person before whom it was sworn,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (4) have the pages numbered consecutively as a separate document (or as one of several documents contained in a file),

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (5) be divided into numbered paragraphs,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (6) have all numbers, including dates, expressed in figures, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] (7) give the reference to any document or documents mentioned either in the margin or in bold text in the body of the affidavit.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 6.1 An affidavit should:] 6.2 It is usually convenient for an affidavit to follow the chronological sequence of events or matters dealt with; each paragraph of an affidavit should as far as possible be confined to a distinct portion of the subject.

## Inability of Deponent to read or sign affidavit

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Inability of Deponent to read or sign affidavit] 7.1 Where an affidavit is sworn by a person who is unable to read or sign it, the person before whom the affidavit is sworn must certify in the jurat that:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Inability of Deponent to read or sign affidavit] (1) he read the affidavit to the deponent,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Inability of Deponent to read or sign affidavit] (2) the deponent appeared to understand it, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Inability of Deponent to read or sign affidavit] (3) the deponent signed or made his mark, in his presence.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Inability of Deponent to read or sign affidavit] 7.2 If that certificate is not included in the jurat, the affidavit may not be used in evidence unless the court is satisfied that it was read to the deponent and that he appeared to understand it. Two versions of the form of jurat with the certificate are set out at Annex 1 to this practice direction.

## Alterations to affidavits

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Alterations to affidavits] 8.1 Any alteration to an affidavit must be initialled by both the deponent and the person before whom the affidavit was sworn.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Alterations to affidavits] 8.2 An affidavit which contains an alteration that has not been initialled may be filed or used in evidence only with the permission of the court.

## Who may administer oaths and take affidavits

## 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (1) a commissioner for oaths 6 ;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (2) omitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (3) other persons specified by statute 7 ;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (4) certain officials of the Senior Courts 8 ;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (5) a circuit judge or district judge 9 ;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (6) any justice of the peace 10 ; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 9.1 Only the following may administer oaths and take affidavits –] (7) certain officials of any county court appointed by the judge of that court for the purpose 11 .

## 9.2 An affidavit must be sworn before a person independent of the parties or their representatives.

## Filing of affidavits

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Filing of affidavits] 10.1 If the court directs that an affidavit is to be filed 12 , it must be filed in the court or Division, or Office or Registry of the court or Division where the action in which it was or is to be used, is proceeding or will proceed.

## 10.2 Where an affidavit is in a foreign language:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 10.2 Where an affidavit is in a foreign language:] (1) the party wishing to rely on it –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 10.2 Where an affidavit is in a foreign language:] (a) must have it translated, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 10.2 Where an affidavit is in a foreign language:] (b) must file the foreign language affidavit with the court, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 10.2 Where an affidavit is in a foreign language:] (2) the translator must make and file with the court an affidavit verifying the translation and exhibiting both the translation and a copy of the foreign language affidavit.

## EXHIBITS

## Manner of exhibiting documents

## 11.1 A document used in conjunction with an affidavit should be:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 11.1 A document used in conjunction with an affidavit should be:] (1) produced to and verified by the deponent, and remain separate from the affidavit, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 11.1 A document used in conjunction with an affidavit should be:] (2) identified by a declaration of the person before whom the affidavit was sworn.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 11.1 A document used in conjunction with an affidavit should be:] 11.2 The declaration should be headed with the name of the proceedings in the same way as the affidavit.

## 11.3 The first page of each exhibit should be marked:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 11.3 The first page of each exhibit should be marked:] (1) as in paragraph 3.2 above, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 11.3 The first page of each exhibit should be marked:] (2) with the exhibit mark referred to in the affidavit.

## Letters

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Letters] 12.1 Copies of individual letters should be collected together and exhibited in a bundle or bundles. They should be arranged in chronological order with the earliest at the top, and firmly secured.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Letters] 12.2 When a bundle of correspondence is exhibited, the exhibit should have a front page attached stating that the bundle consists of original letters and copies. They should be arranged and secured as above and numbered consecutively.

## Other documents

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Other documents] 13.1 Photocopies instead of original documents may be exhibited provided the originals are made available for inspection by the other parties before the hearing and by the judge at the hearing.

## 13.2 Court documents must not be exhibited (official copies of such documents prove themselves).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 13.2 Court documents must not be exhibited (official copies of such documents prove themselves).] 13.3 Where an exhibit contains more than one document, a front page should be attached setting out a list of the documents contained in the exhibit; the list should contain the dates of the documents.

## Exhibits other than documents

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Exhibits other than documents] 14.1 Items other than documents should be clearly marked with an exhibit number or letter in such a manner that the mark cannot become detached from the exhibit.

## 14.2 Small items may be placed in a container and the container appropriately marked.

## General provisions

## 15.1 Where an exhibit contains more than one document:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 15.1 Where an exhibit contains more than one document:] (1) the bundle should not be stapled but should be securely fastened in a way that does not hinder the reading of the documents, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 15.1 Where an exhibit contains more than one document:] (2) the pages should be numbered consecutively at bottom centre.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 15.1 Where an exhibit contains more than one document:] 15.2 Every page of an exhibit should be clearly legible; typed copies of illegible documents should be included, paginated with ‘a’ numbers.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 15.1 Where an exhibit contains more than one document:] 15.3 Where affidavits and exhibits have become numerous, they should be put into separate bundles and the pages numbered consecutively throughout.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 15.1 Where an exhibit contains more than one document:] 15.4 Where on account of their bulk the service of exhibits or copies of exhibits on the other parties would be difficult or impracticable, the directions of the court should be sought as to arrangements for bringing the exhibits to the attention of the other parties and as to their custody pending trial.

## Affirmations

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Affirmations] 16 All provisions in this or any other practice direction relating to affidavits apply to affirmations with the following exceptions:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Affirmations] (1) the deponent should commence ‘I (name) of (address) do solemnly and sincerely affirm ……’, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Affirmations] (2) in the jurat the word ‘sworn’ is replaced by the word ‘affirmed’.

## WITNESS STATEMENTS

## Heading

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Heading] 17.1 The witness statement should be headed with the title of the proceedings (see paragraph 4 of Practice Direction 7A and paragraph 5 of Practice Direction 20); where the proceedings are between several parties with the same status it is sufficient to identify the parties as follows:

## 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:] (1) the party on whose behalf it is made,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:] (2) the initials and surname of the witness,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:] (3) the number of the statement in relation to that witness,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:] (4) the identifying initials and number of each exhibit referred to,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:] (5) the date the statement was made; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 17.2 At the top right hand corner of the first page there should be clearly written:] (6) the date of any translation.

## Body of witness statement

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of witness statement] 18.1 The witness statement must, if practicable, be in the intended witness’s own words and must in any event be drafted in their own language, the statement should be expressed in the first person and should also state:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of witness statement] (1) the full name of the witness,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of witness statement] (2) his place of residence or, if he is making the statement in his professional, business or other occupational capacity, the address at which he works, the position he holds and the name of his firm or employer,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of witness statement] (3) his occupation, or if he has none, his description,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of witness statement] (4) the fact that he is a party to the proceedings or is the employee of such a party if it be the case; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Body of witness statement] (5) the process by which it has been prepared, for example, face-to-face, over the telephone, and/or through an interpreter.

## 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:] (1) which of the statements in it are made from the witness’s own knowledge and which are matters of information or belief, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:] (2) the source for any matters of information or belief.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:] 18.3 An exhibit used in conjunction with a witness statement should be verified and identified by the witness and remain separate from the witness statement.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:] 18.4 Where a witness refers to an exhibit or exhibits, he should state ‘I refer to the (description of exhibit) marked‘…’’.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:] 18.5 The provisions of paragraphs 11.3 to 15.4 (exhibits) apply similarly to witness statements as they do to affidavits.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 18.2 A witness statement must indicate:] 18.6 Where a witness makes more than one witness statement to which there are exhibits, in the same proceedings, the numbering of the exhibits should run consecutively throughout and not start again with each witness statement.

## Format of witness statement

## 19.1 A witness statement should:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (1) be produced on durable quality A4 paper with a 3.5cm margin,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (2) be fully legible and should normally be typed on one side of the paper only,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (3) where possible, be bound securely in a manner which would not hamper filing, or otherwise each page should be endorsed with the case number and should bear the initials of the witness,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (4) have the pages numbered consecutively as a separate statement (or as one of several statements contained in a file),

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (5) be divided into numbered paragraphs,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (6) have all numbers, including dates, expressed in figures,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (7) give the reference to any document or documents mentioned either in the margin or in bold text in the body of the statement ; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] (8) be drafted in the witness’s own language.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 19.1 A witness statement should:] 19.2 It is usually convenient for a witness statement to follow the chronological sequence of the events or matters dealt with, each paragraph of a witness statement should as far as possible be confined to a distinct portion of the subject.

## Statement of Truth

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Statement of Truth] 20.1 A witness statement is the equivalent of the oral evidence which that witness would, if called, give in evidence; it must include a statement by the intended witness in their own language that they believe the facts in it are true 13 .

## 20.2 To verify a witness statement the statement of truth is as follows:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 20.2 To verify a witness statement the statement of truth is as follows:] ‘I believe that the facts stated in this witness statement are true. I understand that proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against anyone who makes, or causes to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth without an honest belief in its truth.’

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 20.2 To verify a witness statement the statement of truth is as follows:] 20.3 Attention is drawn to rule 32.14 which sets out the consequences of verifying a witness statement containing a false statement without an honest belief in its truth.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 20.2 To verify a witness statement the statement of truth is as follows:] (Rule 22.1(9) sets out the procedure to be followed where the person who should sign a document which is verified by a statement of truth is unable to read or sign the document other than by reason of language alone.)

## 21 Omitted

## Alterations to witness statements

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Alterations to witness statements] 22.1 Any alteration to a witness statement must be initialled by the person making the statement or by the authorised person where appropriate (see paragraph 21).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Alterations to witness statements] 22.2 A witness statement which contains an alteration that has not been initialled may be used in evidence only with the permission of the court.

## Filing of witness statements

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Filing of witness statements] 23.1 If the court directs that a witness statement is to be filed 14 , it must be filed in the court or Division, or Office or Registry of the court or Division where the action in which it was or is to be used, is proceeding or will proceed.

## 23.2 Where a witness statement is in a foreign language—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 23.2 Where a witness statement is in a foreign language—] (a) the party wishing to rely on it must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 23.2 Where a witness statement is in a foreign language—] (i) have it translated; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 23.2 Where a witness statement is in a foreign language—] (ii) file the foreign language witness statement with the court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 23.2 Where a witness statement is in a foreign language—] (b) the translator must sign the original statement and must certify that the translation is accurate.

## Certificate of court officer

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > Certificate of court officer] 24.1 Where the court has ordered that a witness statement is not to be open to inspection by the public 15 or that words or passages in the statement are not to be open to inspection 16 the court officer will so certify on the statement and make any deletions directed by the court under rule 32.13(4).

## Defects in affidavits, witness statements and exhibits

## 25.1 Where:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 25.1 Where:] (1) an affidavit,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 25.1 Where:] (2) a witness statement, or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 25.1 Where:] (3) an exhibit to either an affidavit or a witness statement,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 25.1 Where:] does not comply with Part 32 or this practice direction in relation to its form, the court may refuse to admit it as evidence and may refuse to allow the costs arising from its preparation.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 25.1 Where:] 25.2 Permission to file a defective affidavit or witness statement or to use a defective exhibit may be obtained from a judge 17 in the court where the case is proceeding.

## STATEMENTS OF CASE

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > STATEMENTS OF CASE] 26.1 A statement of case may be used as evidence in an interim application provided it is verified by a statement of truth 18 .

## 26.2 To verify a statement of case the statement of truth should be set out as follows:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 32 – EVIDENCE > 26.2 To verify a statement of case the statement of truth should be set out as follows:] ‘[I believe][the (party on whose behalf the statement of case is being signed) believes] that the facts stated in the statement of case are true’.
